label: a8-14-ex-one-point-compactifications-of-the-li
tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_NONFATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/ex-one-point-compactifications-of-the-line-and-of-the-naturals.md, Verification step 4.1, line 101
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: Step 4.1 says “which is a closed bounded interval” and “hence a compact subset” before concluding that the resulting neighbourhood “is open” “by [L1]”.
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: def-one-point-compactification says, “Throughout, "closed" and "compact" without qualification mean closed in $X$ and a compact subset of $X$.” The title of thm-heine-borel-r says, “Heine-Borel by bisection: every closed bounded interval $[a,b]$ is compact”.
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The judge is right that L9 supplies compactness while L1 requires both topological closedness and compactness. The item does not explicitly establish the first condition. This is not fatal under the thirty-second rule: C is the interval from negative M to M, whose complement in the usual topology is the union of the open rays below negative M and above M. The judge does misread def-interval by claiming it contains an explicit disclaimer parallel to def-metric-ball; it contains no such disclaimer, although its interval terminology does not itself prove topological closedness.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
